answer_raw:
MLX is significantly faster for pure inference, while Ollama is the better choice for developer workflows and agent-based tasks.

**MLX** is Apple's native framework and typically runs models at roughly twice the speed of Ollama on the same hardware, such as achieving **60-70+ tok/s** compared to **~35 tok/s** on an M4 Max [3]. For tasks like running agents, Ollama is the preferred choice because it acts as a robust host for multiple users or tools, whereas MLX is better suited for overnight benchmarks [1].

Regarding your 48 GB capacity:

*   **The 30B-35B range** is the comfortable ceiling for your machine; a 48 GB Mac is comfortable up up to about a **30 GB model** on disk [7].
*   **70B models** can technically be loaded using 4-bit quantization (occupying ~43 GB), but they will run at a much slower, less usable speed of roughly **14 tok/s** on an M4 Pro compared to the more comfortable speeds seen on higher-tier chips [4].
*   **Hybrid/MoE models** (like a 35B-A3B) can run very efficiently, but you must be careful with context windows; at a huge 256K context, the KV cache itself can consume massive amounts of memory that might exceed your 48 GB limit [6].

The biggest model you can realistically run is a **70B model** at a quantized level (like Q4_K_M), but it will be pushing your 48 GB limit and will feel slow due to the M4 Pro's bandwidth constraints [4]. For a smooth, productive experience without hitting swap or OOM (Out of Memory) errors while running other apps, sticking to models in the **30B-35B range** is the practical limit [7].
